label: A. J. Ayer, Language Ch: Ayer 1936: by his criterion of significance the assertion that the world…
locator: ch. I, p. 21, "is saying something which, according to our criterion of significance, is literally nonsensical"
interpretation: Ayer's examples of what the 1936 criterion rules out: the unreality thesis, because no conceivable observation could tend to show it, and the monism-pluralism controversy as a whole, since both sides admit no empirical situation could bear on it, so both a thesis and its rival are condemned.
attribution: The passage states that the assertion that the sensible world is unreal is, by his criterion, literally nonsensical, and that the monist-pluralist dispute is fictitious, which is the premise.
